chunks: And from the addition of Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn al-Mughirah, what is in the hadith of Ahmad ibn Idris ibn Ahmad ibn Zakariyya al-Qummi, who said: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Qa'id [Fayd] al-Hannat, from Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the prayer in the two Harams, so he said: 'Pray in full form, even if you pass through it as a traveler.'

key_terms.الْحَرَمَيْنِ: The two holy sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina)

ai.seo_question: Do travelers shorten their prayers in Mecca and Medina?
ai.summary: This hadith from the chain of Ziyadat al-Husayn ibn Ahmad establishes that the sanctity of the two holy shrines (al-Haramayn) overrides the standard traveler's concession of shortening prayers (Qasr). The Imam specifies that even a mere passerby must perform full (Tamam) prayers, emphasizing the unique spiritual status of these locations where the traveler's temporary state does not diminish the completeness of worship.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 9. Ḥusain ibn Aḥmad ibn Mughīrah (the student of the author) added the following: Aḥmad ibn Idrīs ibn Aḥmad ibn Zakariyyā Al-Qummi narrated from Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdil Jabbār, from ‘Ali ibn Ismā’īl, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Amr, from Qā`id Al-Ḥannāť, who said:
I asked Abal Ḥasan Al-Māďi (Imam Kāżim (a.s.)) about establishing prayers in the two Ḥarams. Imam (a.s.) replied, “Establish prayers in full form even if you are passing through (Makkah or Madīnah).”
